speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please tell me how long you have been experiencing this chronic cough, weight loss, and weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent release from prison and these systemic symptoms, have you experienced any exposure to tuberculosis or noticed any blood in your sputum? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of diabetes or HIV, and have you traveled to or lived in areas where tuberculosis or fungal infections are common? REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Acid_Fast_Bacilli_Smear

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the AFB smear was normal despite the clinical suspicion and diffuse infiltrates, I need to rule out other causes like malignancy or fungal infection. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest REQUEST TEST: HIV_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal HIV and CT results, I need to broaden the differential to include atypical infections or malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Galactomannan REQUEST TEST: Serum_Beta_D_Glucan

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative results for TB, HIV, and common fungal markers despite diffuse infiltrates and significant weight loss, I need to evaluate for other opportunistic infections or malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Bronchoscopy_with_BAL REQUEST TEST: Serum_GALACTOMANNAN_REQUEST_AGAIN

speaker: Doctor
text: Since bronchoscopy and fungal markers are negative, we must look towards malignancy or other granulomatous diseases. REQUEST TEST: PET_CTD REQUEST TEST: Serum_Calcium

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal PET-CT and calcium levels, we must now consider non-infectious inflammatory conditions or rare malignancies that may not show metabolic activity on PET. I need to check for autoimmune involvement and lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: ANA_REQUEST REQUEST TEST: LDH

speaker: Doctor
text: With extensive negative workup for infection, malignancy, and autoimmune disease, I must consider non-caseating granulomatous diseases like sarcoidosis or atypical presentations of lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Angiotensin_Converting_Enzyme REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Angiotensin Converting Enzyme: Elevated; Images: Generalized Lymphadenopathy Present, Hepatomegaly Present, Three discrete, yellow-colored, 0.5 mm to 1.0 mm lesions with indistinct borders in the posterior pole

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated ACE levels, generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, and ocular lesions are classic findings for sarcoidosis, despite the atypical presentation and negative malignancy workup. DIAGNOSIS READY: Sarcoidosis
